segments.title: Planning a focused research path for D-class cruisers
segments.body: A D-class cruiser research project starts by defining the class as its subject. Book indexes and recognizable ship names can then identify relevant material without reading every apparently useful volume from cover to cover. In this example, that reduces one large book to a single useful page and excludes sources that do not address the class. A balanced encyclopedia entry of several pages becomes the key text, providing a foundation for further reading without overwhelming the project with technical detail. The research plan controls source selection before writing begins.

evidence.note: Narrowing a D-class cruiser project through indexes, recognizable ship names, relevant pages, and a balanced key text.

segments.summary: A precise D-class cruiser question, book indexes, and a balanced key text turn a large naval-history library into a manageable research path.
